clinicalPearls: Characterised by the triad of cone-shaped phalangeal epiphyses, nephronophthisis (chronic tubulointerstitial kidney disease) and retinal dystrophy
Cone-shaped epiphyses are best seen on hand radiographs and give the condition its alternative name of conorenal syndrome
The retinal dystrophy resembles a rod-cone dystrophy or Leber congenital amaurosis and may precede renal signs
Nephronophthisis presents with polyuria, polydipsia, anaemia and growth failure before progressing to end-stage renal disease
Cerebellar ataxia and mild vermis changes may accompany the renal and retinal features
Considered part of the nephronophthisis-related ciliopathy spectrum, overlapping with Senior-Loken and Jeune syndromes
Caused by biallelic variants in intraflagellar transport genes, notably IFT140 and IFT172
reference.pathophysiology: Mainzer-Saldino syndrome is caused by biallelic variants in intraflagellar transport genes, particularly IFT140 and IFT172, whose products carry cargo along the primary cilium. Impaired ciliary transport disturbs the specialised sensory cilia of retinal photoreceptors, the primary cilia of renal tubular epithelium and the signalling that governs epiphyseal cartilage, producing the retinal dystrophy, nephronophthisis and cone-shaped phalangeal epiphyses respectively. The same ciliary dependence in the cerebellum accounts for the ataxia seen in some individuals. The condition therefore sits within the wider group of nephronophthisis-related ciliopathies, sharing mechanisms with Senior-Loken and Jeune syndromes while showing milder skeletal change than the short-rib thoracic dysplasias.
additionalDifferentials: Tricho-rhino-phalangeal syndrome (other causes of cone-shaped epiphyses)
additionalInvestigations: Hand and skeletal radiographs to identify cone-shaped epiphyses
Renal function testing, urine concentrating ability and renal ultrasound
Electroretinography and ophthalmological assessment for retinal dystrophy
Brain imaging for cerebellar vermis changes when ataxia is present
Molecular testing with a nephronophthisis / ciliopathy gene panel
redFlags: Progressive renal impairment towards end-stage disease
Growth failure and anaemia from renal disease
Cerebellar signs indicating central nervous system involvement
reference.prognosis: Renal failure typically develops during childhood or adolescence and requires dialysis or transplantation, while visual loss from retinal dystrophy is variable but may be severe; overall outlook is largely determined by the renal course.
pitfalls: Attributing early visual loss to isolated retinal disease and missing the progressive nephropathy
Overlooking subtle cone-shaped epiphyses on hand radiographs
Failing to monitor renal concentrating ability so that nephronophthisis is recognised late
Not distinguishing it from other nephronophthisis-related ciliopathies without genetic testing
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: No disease-specific therapy exists, so management targets the individual organ manifestations of this ciliopathy

Manage progressive nephronophthisis and chronic kidney disease with blood pressure control, correction of anaemia, growth support and fluid-electrolyte balance, progressing to dialysis and renal transplantation
Ophthalmological management of the retinal dystrophy with low-vision aids and visual rehabilitation
Nutritional and growth support, treating the polyuria and polydipsia and addressing growth failure
Orthopaedic assessment of the cone-shaped epiphyseal skeletal changes and monitoring for cerebellar ataxia
Multidisciplinary long-term care coordinated across paediatric nephrology, ophthalmology and genetics
Genetic counselling and family screening for this autosomal recessive intraflagellar-transport disorder (IFT140/IFT172)
